title.en: Types of triangles and the exterior angle

text.en:
Meena folded a paper triangle and tore off its corners to put them together.
"They make a straight line," she said.

Triangles can be named by sides: equilateral (all equal), isosceles (two equal) and scalene (none equal). By angles they are acute, right or obtuse.
The three angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees. An exterior angle is formed by extending one side, and it equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles.
So if two interior angles are 50 and 60 degrees, the third is 70 and the exterior angle at it is 110.

prompt.en: A friend says the angles of a triangle add up to 360. How will you reply?
